title: When Dreams Merge
subtitle: A Collection of Verse
author: Gajendra Thakur
summary: An expansive collection in which dream and waking life become a threshold for questions about time, selfhood, language, society, knowledge and liberation. Early sections move between memory, folk life, home and modern social experience; later sections turn increasingly toward language, philosophical traditions and competing accounts of truth, cause, consciousness, duty, history and justice. The annex shifts into two extended song cycles: the eighteen-parva “You and I” and the twenty-eight-canto “The Unborn Mind”. Across the volume, impermanence is not treated as an argument for withdrawal: inward freedom repeatedly stands beside responsibility toward suffering, social life and the changing world.
method: Concise editorial summaries prepared from the complete uploaded 2026 revised English volume. Section overviews were written after reading each section as a whole; individual entries are source-grounded thematic summaries derived from the corresponding poem, sequence, parva or canto. PDF page numbers include front matter.
